message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I'm p1 with $382 cash. I'm on INCOME_TAX. All light blue properties are mortgaged. Pinks have 2 houses each. Oranges have 4 houses each. I hold one GOOJF card.

p2 has $345 and owns reds with 3/3/4 houses. p4 has $126 and owns yellows with 1/1/2 houses. p3 is bankrupt. The bank holds 0 houses and 12 hotels. North Carolina Avenue is unowned.

I'm weighing whether to build hotels on St. James, Tennessee, and New York. Each hotel costs $100 and returns four houses to the bank. p2 could then buy those houses for their red properties.

Building a hotel on an orange would return four houses to the bank. p2 could then even out their reds to 4/4/4 for $300. That would be devastating. Illinois is already at four houses.

I've decided against building hotels. Unmortgaging the light blues would cost too much and yield almost no rent.

I need the $382 cash buffer to cover Marvin Gardens at two houses, which costs $360. I'm now considering whether to trade for something useful.

Trading is unlikely to help. p2 and p4 are not going to give up their orange or pink properties for cash. p4 is on SHORT_LINE, so he pays no rent there. p2 is on WATER_WORKS, which is mortgaged. The housing lock remains the core strategy.

p4's liquid assets total roughly $450. That includes four yellow houses sold for $300, plus cash and mortgage value. An orange property with four houses pays $750 to $800 in rent. p4 cannot survive that hit without selling everything and likely going bankrupt. p2 has $345 in cash plus red houses worth $750 and Boardwalk at $200.

I'm now considering proposing a trade to hurt p2 or p4, but rejected offers waste one of my twenty available exchanges. I'll likely just end the turn.
